Reservoir launches Washington agricultural robotics incubator with grower partners

The initiative links developers, WSU researchers and growers for field testing, with the new site details still to be announced.

The Robot Report ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A new field-testing network

Reservoir announced a Washington agricultural robotics incubator with Washington State University’s IAREC in Prosser, the Washington Tree Fruit Research Commission and the Tri-City Development Council. It connects startups, researchers and growers around technology for agricultural production.

Development around real crops

Developers are to gain access to orchards, vineyards and berry fields to address labor costs and workforce constraints. Washington crops include apples, cherries, pears, blueberries, wine grapes and hops. Working with growers enables evaluation under real operating conditions beyond laboratory demonstrations.

New site details are still pending

The Washington site details have not been announced. The 24-acre location and innovation barns mentioned in the source belong to the existing Salinas, California base pictured in the article. The new incubator expands testing access; it does not establish commercial validation or savings for a particular robot.
